title: The board no longer loses a click while the ship loads, and recurring flaky tests are root-caused instead of only rerun
public_title: Stop the ship panel from moving the tabs, and investigate repeat flakes
acceptance: Why. One end-to-end test has failed on its own several times with no related code change: `tests/e2e/board-task-detail.spec.ts`, 'external review locations and minute refresh stay private'. It failed in CI on pull request #254 (head c0e9d5ac, run 37914100220, job 113765977729), #250 (head f850ca5e, run 37940259051, job 113852530788) and #257 (head 0a827688, run 37944436357, job 113866939723), and once in 30 local runs on main 394cf75. Each time a rerun passed, so each time it was rerun and nothing was learned, and each failure held a merge for one CI round. The CI log always shows the same thing: the beta/T-001 card exists on the page, but Playwright reports 'element is not visible' from its very first attempt until the 60-second timeout. The card sits in the Fleet tab's panel (`#fleetPanel`), so that panel never became visible.

Root cause, proved. The voyage stage is the iframe that shows the ship. `board/public/game.js` puts its panel above the counts and the tab bar (line 45) and loads the iframe only after the board's first render, in an idle callback (`mountLater`, lines 52-70). Until then its box, `#voyage-mount`, is empty and 0 px tall. When the iframe arrives it is as tall as `#voyage-stage` (`board/public/index.html` line 203), so everything below it, the tab bar included, jumps down. If that jump happens between the mouse press and the mouse release of a click on the Fleet tab, the press and the release land on different elements, the browser sends no click to the Fleet button, `selectTab('fleet')` (index.html about line 986) never runs, and `#fleetPanel` stays hidden for good. This is a product bug: a captain who clicks a tab while the board is still loading loses the click the same way. The test makes it more likely only because it installs Playwright's fake clock (`page.clock.install`), which turns the idle callback into a fake-clock timer that fires later, closer to the click.

Evidence. Every run below used Playwright 1.63.0 in the image mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble on main a118b06 with one probe added before the click (`state/session/T274-flaky/evidence/probe-instrumentation.diff`). These files are firstmate's private local evidence; the reviewer does not need them, because acceptance lines 6 and 7 reproduce the cause deterministically in CI. (a) E3: the iframe forced to mount at the first mouse press (`experiment-e3.diff`) fails 20 of 20 runs with the exact CI message; the probe shows `#fleetPanel` hidden and the Fleet tab not selected, and `shots/e3-at-fail-1.png` shows the ship mounted, the tab bar pushed down and Decisions still selected (`out-e3.txt`). (b) E4: the same forced timing plus the reserved box (`experiment-e4.diff`) passes 20 of 20 (`out-e4.txt`). (c) E5: the reserved box alone passes 100 of 100 under load, 4 workers on 2 CPUs (`out-e5.txt`). (d) Unforced runs on main did not fail in 140 runs, which is why the forced experiment is the proof. Reproduce with `run2.sh`: `docker run --cpus=2 -e N=10 -e W=2 -e SRC=src-e3 -e SPECS=tests/e2e/board-task-detail.spec.ts:127 -v <dir>:/f mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble bash /f/run2.sh`.

How. Reserve the stage's space before the iframe exists, so loading it never moves anything below it. Whenever the stage is shown and the voyage is not full screen, `#voyage-mount` already has exactly the height its iframe will have. When the voyage is hidden (the double-Esc preference), nothing is reserved, as today. Full screen keeps its existing geometry. Nothing else about the voyage changes: when and how it loads, its sizes, its keys and its iframe stay the same. No JavaScript change and no timer.

Product change, the four sizes. The reserved minimum height equals the iframe height in each non-full-screen size: desktop panel `clamp(270px, 36vh, 440px)` (`board/public/index.html` line 203); narrow panel 270 px (the `max-width:650px` rule at index.html lines 222-225); desktop strip 88 px and narrow strip 72 px (`board/public/board.css` lines 38-40). The rules live next to the iframe rules they mirror, in those two files.

Product change, full screen untouched. The new rule must not apply in full screen: it is scoped with `:not(.voyage-full *)`, the pattern the strip rule already uses (board.css line 38), so `.voyage-full #voyage-mount{min-height:0}` (index.html line 209) still wins and the full-screen grid keeps its shape at every width and height.

Deterministic test, layout. A new file, `tests/e2e/voyage-layout.spec.ts`, holds the fake clock paused from before the board's page loads, after the fixture's sign-in navigation (`tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts` about line 284), so the stage's idle callback cannot fire. For each of four cases, desktop panel (1280x720), narrow panel (390x844), desktop strip and narrow strip, it asserts that the iframe is absent, records the tab bar's position and `#voyage-mount`'s height, lets the clock run until the iframe is present, and asserts that the tab bar did not move and that `#voyage-mount`'s height equals the iframe's height. On main this fails because the tab bar moves down by the iframe height; that is the fail-first.

Deterministic test, the lost click. The same file presses the mouse on the Fleet tab, lets the paused clock run so the iframe mounts while the button is held, releases the mouse, and asserts that the Fleet tab is selected and `#fleetPanel` is visible. On main this fails because the click is lost; with the change it passes. It uses only Playwright's mouse and clock APIs and adds no test hook to product code.

Deterministic test, hidden and full screen. The same file asserts that with the voyage hidden (localStorage `board.voyage.hidden` is `1`) `#voyage-mount` is hidden and takes no space, and that in full screen at 1280x720 and at 390x500 the iframe still fills `#voyage-mount` and nothing overflows the viewport.

Fail fast instead of waiting 60 seconds. `showFleet` in `tests/e2e/lib/board.ts` (lines 82-87) clicks the Fleet tab and then asserts that the tab is selected (`aria-selected` is `true`) and `#fleetPanel` is visible. Its signature does not change. If a click is ever lost again, every caller fails at that line with a clear message instead of timing out later on an invisible card. It does not retry the click, because a retry would hide the bug. There are 42 call sites in 14 files under `tests/e2e/`; none needs an edit.

No timeout or retry changes. `tests/e2e/board-task-detail.spec.ts` is not changed: its fake clock stays, because its minute-refresh checks need it. `playwright.config.ts` keeps zero retries and its timeouts.

Rerun rule (captain, 2026-09-30, now written down). `skills/firstmate/SKILL.md` allows firstmate to rerun only the failed jobs of a CI run, `gh run rerun <run> --failed`, when a failure is shown to be flaky: the same code passed that job before, or nothing the pull request changed can reach the failing test. Both places that today call `gh pr update-branch` the only `gh` command firstmate runs (the opening paragraph, line 14, and Process rule 2, line 521) are updated to name these two commands and their conditions.

Recurring flakes are root-caused (captain, 2026-10-09). The same Process rule says: the second time one flaky signature is seen, firstmate starts a root-cause investigation by a separate researcher, a stock read-only research round or a delegated agent, which reproduces the failure, proves the cause with a controlled experiment and writes a fix task spec for the captain. A rerun may still unblock the pull request meanwhile. An investigation already open for that signature is never started twice.

Rerun evidence, published only where allowed. When the project's projection setting allows pull request comments, a rerun gets a comment naming the job, the evidence and, from the second hit on, the open investigation. On an external project (`FM_EXTERNAL=1`) firstmate follows that project's projection and conventions and never publishes private project text, spec text or research findings; the evidence stays in the private ledger.

Flaky signature. A signature is the repository, the test file, the test title with any trailing parameter in parentheses removed (so 'external review locations … (en)' and '… (zh-TW)' are one signature), and the error class, for example 'locator.click timeout: element is not visible'. The repository is the GitHub `owner/name` from the project's `github` setting in `config.yaml` (for this repository `BenjaminLu/firstmate-workflow`), never the local project key; the ledger also stores the project key, but only to find the state root. Line numbers are not part of a signature. Two failures with the same signature are the same flake on any pull request or head; the same test title under another `owner/name`, including another owner with the same repository name, is a different flake.

Flaky ledger, the helper. A new helper, `bin/lib/fm_flaky.py`, owns one JSON ledger per project state root. It chooses the root with the existing routing, `record_root` in `bin/lib/fm_project_paths.py` (lines 119-192), driven by `--project <name>` (default: the default project): `<root>/state/flaky-ledger.json` for this repository and the external project's private storage root for an external one. If an external project's root cannot be resolved it exits 65 and writes nothing; it never falls back to the engine's `state/`. Every command names the signature with `--repo owner/name --file <path> --title <title> --error <class>` (the title is normalised as in the signature rule). Examples: `fm_flaky.py hit --project firstmate-workflow --repo BenjaminLu/firstmate-workflow --file tests/e2e/game.spec.ts --title '…' --error 'expect toHaveCount timeout' --pr 254 --head 394dde1d --run 37914880158 --job 113768525915 --attempt 1 --at 2026-10-09T10:13:07Z`; `investigate … --owner firstmate`; `link … --task T-275`; `fixed … --pr 260 --commit <sha>`; `show [--project <name>]`. Writes are atomic (temporary file and rename); a missing ledger starts empty.

Flaky ledger, the format. The file is `{"schema": 1, "signatures": [...]}`. Each signature entry has `repository`, `project`, `file`, `title`, `error_class`, `first_seen` (the earliest hit's `at`), `hits` and `investigation`. A hit is `{pr, head, run, job, attempt, at, rerun}`; `at` is the CI job's completion time that firstmate passes in, never the time of recording. One failure is identified by repository, run, job and attempt: recording it again changes nothing, except that `hit … --rerun` on an existing hit sets its `rerun` flag. A rerun that fails again is a new attempt and so a new hit. The investigation is `{status, owner, task, merged_pr, merge_commit, fixed_at}`, with status `none`, `open`, `fix-task` or `fixed`; `open` and `fix-task` are active. `fixed_at` is the fix's merge time that firstmate passes in with `fixed … --at`. Earlier investigations are kept, unchanged, in a `history` list on the entry. The current cycle is every hit whose `at` is later than the last `fixed_at`; a signature never fixed has all its hits in the current cycle. `show` and `hit` report the current cycle's hit count, which is the count the second-hit rule uses. Unknown fields are kept when the file is rewritten.

Flaky ledger, the lifecycle. `investigate` moves `none` or `fixed` to `open` and refuses (exit 65, nothing written) while the signature is active, that is `open` or `fix-task`; starting from `fixed` first moves the finished investigation into `history`, so its task, pull request and merge commit are kept; `link` moves `open` to `fix-task` and records the task id; `fixed` moves `fix-task` (or `open`) to `fixed` and records the merged pull request and merge commit. A new hit on a `fixed` signature reopens nothing by itself: it starts a new cycle, and the second distinct hit of that cycle triggers the second-hit rule. The ledger is new, so no record predates `fixed_at`: a `fixed` record without `fixed_at` is invalid, and every command refuses it (exit 65, the file unchanged, a message naming the signature) instead of guessing a cutoff. There is no import of free-text notes: firstmate's current notes file, `state/session/T-179-flaky-observations.md`, is prose and is not parsed. After this task merges, firstmate records the known hits below with `hit`, checks them with `show`, and only then deletes that notes file. These are firstmate's own actions on its private state; the worker writes no ledger file and no state file.

Flaky ledger, this task's entries. After merging, firstmate records, with repository `BenjaminLu/firstmate-workflow` and project `firstmate-workflow`: (1) `tests/e2e/board-task-detail.spec.ts`, 'external review locations and minute refresh stay private', error 'locator.click timeout: element is not visible', hits #254 c0e9d5ac run 37914100220 job 113765977729 attempt 1 at 2026-10-09T09:57:35Z, #250 f850ca5e run 37940259051 job 113852530788 attempt 1 at 2026-10-09T13:59:31Z, #257 0a827688 run 37944436357 job 113866939723 attempt 1 at 2026-10-09T14:34:47Z, each rerun; investigation owner firstmate, task T-274, then `fixed` with this task's merged pull request and merge commit. (2) `tests/e2e/game.spec.ts`, 'voyage is one live stage, persists its size, and Esc Esc unloads it', error 'expect toHaveCount timeout', hit #254 394dde1d run 37914880158 job 113768525915 attempt 1 at 2026-10-09T10:13:07Z, rerun; investigation `open`, owner firstmate. Its cause is already shown and is out of scope here: the test presses Escape twice with an awaited assertion between them (lines 23-25, and again at 30), and under CPU load the two presses land more than 400 ms apart, outside the double-press window in `board/public/game.js` line 106. firstmate's private evidence: a trace with the presses 494 ms apart (`state/session/T274-flaky/evidence/game-esc-trace.zip`), the original test failing 26 of 30 runs with 6 workers on 2 CPUs (`out-load1.txt`), and the test with the page clock paused around each pair passing 40 of 40 under the same load (`experiment-e2.diff`, `out-e2b.txt`). firstmate raises its fix task card after this task's card is answered and records it with `link`.

Tests for the helper. `tests/flaky-ledger.test.sh` with `tests/lib/flaky_ledger.py` and fixtures in `tests/fixtures/flaky-ledger/` cover, each as a named assertion: a first hit creates an entry whose `first_seen` is the hit's `at`, not the clock; a second hit with another line number and the other locale suffix joins the same signature and the hit count is 2; recording the same run, job and attempt twice keeps one hit, and `--rerun` only sets its flag; a later attempt of the same job is a second hit; the same title under another `owner/name` with the same repository name stays separate; `investigate` refuses while `open` and, after `link`, while `fix-task`; `link` and `fixed` persist the task id, pull request and merge commit; `show` prints every signature with its hit count and status; a ledger fixture with pre-existing hits and an active investigation is read correctly, counts its hits toward the second-hit rule and refuses a new investigation; an external project resolves to its private root, and an unresolvable external project exits 65 and writes nothing anywhere; unknown fields survive a rewrite; after `fixed --at`, the first new hit gives a current-cycle count of 1 and the second gives 2, also when the second is recorded by a new process that only reads the file; recording the same post-fix hit twice keeps the count at 1; `investigate` from `fixed` opens a new investigation and keeps the earlier one in `history`; a fixture `fixed` record without `fixed_at` makes `hit`, `show` and `investigate` exit 65 and leaves the file byte for byte unchanged. These fail on main because the helper does not exist; that absence is a skip, never counted as behavioural evidence, and each named assertion is behavioural on the new code.

Skill contract tests. `tests/skills-contract.test.sh` gains contracts for the new rule: rerun only of failed jobs and only when shown flaky; the second hit of a signature, counting hits already in the ledger, starts an independent investigation with a controlled experiment and a fix spec; an active investigation (open or fix task) is never started twice; a rerun comment names the open investigation; external projects keep evidence private and follow their projection; the rule applies from this task's merge for sessions that reloaded the skills; the ledger path, the helper name and its commands. Each contract fails on main, where the rule is absent.

When the rule starts. The rule applies from the merge of this task onward, for every firstmate session that has reloaded the merged skills. Hits seeded from the notes count toward the second-hit threshold, so a signature already seen twice starts its investigation at the next hit unless one is already open. Existing task pins, review receipts, decisions and events are unchanged; open pull requests need no action.

Design. `design/design.md` §8, in the subsection '### T-125: Live voyage seam', gains one sentence: the stage's box is reserved at its final height before the iframe loads, so loading the ship never moves the counts, the tabs or anything below them. The edit stays inside that subsection.

Regression. Every existing end-to-end test and every other suite stay green, including the voyage tests in `tests/e2e/game.spec.ts` (size toggle, strip size, full screen, the idle-mount check at line 54, the double-Esc hide) and the size checks in `tests/e2e/board-v2-shell.spec.ts` (lines 73, 89, 126). The board at 390 px wide still has no horizontal overflow (`board-task-detail.spec.ts:65`).
